prerequisites: Completion of the study entry and orientation phase
Completion of elective module A1 or A2 (5 ECTS-AP total) depending on chosen specialization

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to apply the acquired knowledge and competences in sub-areas of mechatronics to correctly solve practical problems in industrial mechatronics and material sciences.
They are familiar with the necessary theoretical foundations, methods, and theories and know their application possibilities and limitations.
They are able to adequately document and discuss elaborated results and solutions.

syllabus_topics: Probability theory and statistics for electrical engineering/mechatronics: concept of probability, discrete and continuous probability spaces, conditional probability, independence, random variables and their distributions, expectations and variance, correlation, central limit theorem, confidence intervals, parameter tests

Theoretical foundations of computer science: propositional logic, automata theory and application, regular languages, formalizing languages/grammars, syntax and semantics in languages, computability, Turing machine, halting problem and decidability, complexity of algorithms, P and NP classes, solution methods for NP problems

Circuit technology: fundamentals of analog electronic circuits, large and small signal analysis of circuits, basic transistor circuits, current mirrors and current sources, structure and function of differential amplifiers with resistive and active loads, structure of operational amplifiers, basic op-amp circuits
Simulation in control engineering: fundamentals and application of various software tools for simulating dynamic systems

Fundamentals of digital image analysis: properties of digital images, noise and blur, point operations, spatial domain filtering, mathematical morphology, discrete Fourier and wavelet transformations, frequency domain filtering, deconvolution, application examples
Practical experience in mechatronics: reporting and discussing experiences from a minimum 240-hour practical training in the technical field of mechatronics
Mechatronics - selected topics: alternately offered courses on special module-relevant topics
